newsitem.title: UK: Minutes-George sees case for future rate rises.
newsitem.headline: Minutes-George sees case for future rate rises.

text.p: Bank of England governor Eddie George said October's interest rate rise may not be enough to bring inflation down to the government's target, minutes from the October 30 monetary meeting showed.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and George agreed to push up interest rates by a quarter percentage point to six percent on October 30.
"He wanted to stay ahead of the game again this time, and he was inclined to agree with the governor's recommendation to move interest rates up," the minutes said.
Clarke saw no reason for delay but also no case for a larger rise, the minutes said.
Clarke said the fact that GDP had accelerated and was likely to continue accelerating was "very relevant to the decision on interest rates".
"Although there were still no immediate inflationary pressures, Clarke said he wanted to ensure that the inflation target was met in 18 months' to two years' time."
The recovery was still not completely uniform, Clarke said. He expected retailers to have a good Christmas, but so no sign of an excessive consumer boom.

George saw evidence that some retailers were seeking to restore margins. "The prudent assumption was that in some part at least recent stronger-than-expected RPIX inflation would persist," the minutes quoted George as saying.

He said arguments that the pound's rise represented a monetary tightening were flawed. "It did nothing directly to address the accelerating upswing in domestic demand and now output," George was quoted as saying.
To that extent, George said, the stronger pound did not do much to improve the chances of hitting the inflation target.
Sterling has risen sharply against the mark and dollar since August.
Clarke said he had wanted to wait for the first estimate of third-quarter GDP growth before making a decision on interest rates. He said he was inclined to believe the 0.8 percent estimate of growth.
